title: One Thread or Many: Executors, Callback Groups and the Control Loop Stuck Behind the Planner

questions.question: A planner callback takes 50 ms and a control callback runs every 10 ms on the same single thread. What happens to the control loop?
options: It is held up by up to 45 ticks while the planner runs, and a planner of 200 ticks held it up by 195
It is dropped while the planner runs, and 5 control callbacks never happen
It preempts the planner, so the planner takes 45 ticks longer
It runs on time, since a 10 ms callback is queued ahead of a 50 ms one
questions.explanation: One thread runs one callback at a time, in the order they became ready. The control callback waits for whatever is in front of it.

questions.question: What does two threads with the control and the planner in separate groups give the control callback?
options: A worst wait of 45 ticks, as with one thread
A worst wait of 22 ticks, half of one thread's
A worst wait of 5 ticks, the planner's start time
0: it runs on time, while the planner runs beside it
questions.explanation: With a thread free and nothing in its group to exclude it, the control callback starts the moment it is ready.

questions.question: Everything is in one mutually exclusive group and the executor has two threads. What is the worst wait?
options: 0: a second thread always removes the wait
45, exactly what one thread gave: callbacks in one exclusive group never overlap, and the second thread sits idle
22, half of what one thread gave
90, twice what one thread gave, from contention
questions.explanation: A mutually exclusive group runs one of its callbacks at a time however many threads there are. The planner still blocks the control.

questions.question: What does making the group reentrant cost?
options: Nothing: reentrant is exclusive with the waiting removed
The callbacks of that group can now run at once, so whatever they share needs a lock: the race the exclusive group was preventing
A thread for each callback in the group
The order of delivery within a topic
questions.explanation: The exclusive group was what guaranteed its callbacks never touched shared data together. Remove it and the callbacks have to protect that data themselves.

questions.question: Four 10 tick callbacks are ready together in a reentrant group on two threads. When do they start?
options: 0 0 10 10: a group that allows overlap still has only as many threads as there are
0 0 0 0: reentrant means no waiting
0 10 20 30: one at a time, in order
0 5 10 15: the threads share each callback
questions.explanation: Two threads run two callbacks. The other two start when those finish; with three threads the third started at once.

questions.question: A callback blocked by its group is ahead of one in another group in the queue. What happens to the second?
options: It waits too, since the queue is served strictly in order
It is dropped, to keep the queue from growing
It runs at once: a blocked callback does not hold up those behind it, and one that never started is reported as having waited the whole time
It is moved into the blocked callback's group
questions.explanation: A callback that cannot run because of its group is passed over for the next one that can. And one that never started is counted as waiting until the end, or the measure would hide it.
